## Exa Lite

Exa 3.0 also includes Exa Lite, our new search type, priced at $4 per 1,000 requests.

Lite runs on the same index as Exa Auto. For higher quality, Exa Auto uses more compute across the retrieval stack, including candidate generation, highlights, and ranking.

For cost-sensitive applications, Lite offers strong search quality at a lower price. Together, Lite and Auto set a new Pareto frontier for search.

...

## Availability

Exa 3.0 is available today through the API, including Exa Lite, upgraded highlights, and our expanded index. Exa Lite costs $4 per 1,000 requests, Exa Auto is $7 per 1,000 requests, and the improved highlights and expanded data sources are included at no additional charge.

results.title: Exa Search API
highlights:
Choose a search type

`type` selects a search mode, each tuned for a different balance of speed, search depth, and synthesis. `auto` is the default and works for most searches.

| Type | Use it when | Typical latency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auto` | You want the best default balance of quality and speed | ~1 second |
| `fast` | The request is latency-sensitive | ~450 ms |
| `instant` | The request is on a real-time path such as autocomplete or voice | ~250 ms |
| `deep-lite` | The task needs lightweight research and synthesis | ~4 seconds |
| `deep` | The task requires multi-step search and stronger synthesis | 4–15 seconds |
| `deep-reasoning` | Completeness and reasoning depth matter more than latency | 12–40 seconds |

`instant` costs $4 per 1,000 requests with up to 10 results. Latency figures are approximate and cover the search itself with cached content. `outputSchema` adds a synthesis step and a low `contents.maxAgeHours` adds a fresh page fetch; see Budget latency and context. Deep modes run a research process rather than a single retrieval pass. See Deep Search for how that process works and how to use its additional controls.

Instead of `deep-reasoning`, use Exa Agent for long-running research, list building, and multi-hop enrichment. Agent has more compute per run and returns grounded, structured results.

Content options for text, highlights, summary, extras, and freshness controls.

Additional query variations for deep-search variants. Only works with a deep-search type. When provided, these queries are used alongside the main query for broader results.

Required array length: `1 - 10` elements

auto · string lite · string deep-lite · string deep · string instant · string fast · string deep-reasoning · string Other values · string

The search mode to use. Defaults to `auto`, a balanced mode recommended for most applications.

- `auto`: The default. A balanced mode that optimizes for both quality and speed and is recommended for most applications.
- `lite`: Low-cost, low-latency search for real-time and interactive experiences such as chat, voice agents, and autocomplete. Accepts only `query` (a single string), `objective`, `userIdentifier`, `metadata`, `category`, `numResults`, `contents.highlights`, `contents.text`, `contents.snapshotAsOf`, `userLocation`, `includeDomains`, `excludeDomains`, `startPublishedDate`, `endPublishedDate`, `moderation`, and `compliance`; a request that sets any other parameter is rejected. Serves cached content only; it never fetches live, so the freshness options are rejected.
- `deep-lite`: Performs lightweight research with synthesized results and a consistent 4-second latency, lower than full deep search.
- `deep`: Conducts comprehensive multi-step research with synthesis.
- `instant`: Legacy. Use `lite` instead. Runs a minimum-latency search that trades some search depth for speed. Unlike `lite`, it accepts every search parameter.
- `fast`: Legacy. Use `lite` instead. Runs a reduced-latency search for user-facing and interactive workflows. Unlike `lite`, it accepts every search parameter.
- `deep-reasoning`: Legacy. Use `deep` instead. Runs `deep` with stronger reasoning at each step, for complex analysis and decision-making tasks. For agentic, multi-step research, use the Agent API.

Allowed value: `"auto"`

A data category to focus on. Other strings are accepted and used as category hints. `people` and `company` return higher-quality people profiles and company pages. `publication` returns scholarly publications such as research papers, preprints, and journal articles, with ... like authors, venue, and citations. ... company` and `people` ... not support ... PublishedDate` or `endPublishedDate`, and `people` also does not support `excludeDomains`. Requests that set an unsupported filter return a 400 error
